When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall

Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session

Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. ## Context

  (Lean 4, no Mathlib). Build from `formal/` with `~/.elan/bin/lake`.

  clause numbers are those of v0, with the new item §63.9. v0 is history: never cite it.

  Read the clauses you touch in the v0.1 file and the arbitration file before editing.
- Previous obligation map (v0 era, for orientation only): `SP/table-final.md`.

## Hard rules (in addition to AGENTS.md)

- No `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide`, `noncomputable`, `set_option`. No warnings.
- Every constant's axioms must be within {propext, Quot.sound}. `Classical.choice` is NOT allowed. Avoid
  `Classical`, `by_contra` on non-decidable props, `Decidable.byContradiction` on classical instances,
  `simp` lemmas that pull `Classical.choice` (check if unsure with `#print axioms` in a scratch file
  under `SP/`).
- Every def/theorem docstring cites the clause it formalizes (`§63.9`, `§69.2`, ...). Module headers that
  name the spec file must name `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`.
- Everything in English. Do not commit; do not touch git state (no stash, checkout, reset).
- Never weaken a statement, never add an unjustified hypothesis, never change a definition to make a
  proof go through. If a proof is stuck on a goal you believe false, build a concrete counterexample
  (a `decide`-checked state) if you can, stop and report the goal state.
- New helper lemmas you add to a file that other agents do not own must be `private` or carry a
  file-specific prefix, so that two files never define the same public name.

## Fixed design (decided by the orchestrator; do not deviate, report instead)

D1 Pinning obligations (v0.1 §74, §75; arbitration Q23 B#45).
  - In `Basic.lean`, add
    `structure PinOb where place : Nat; leaves : List Nat; active : Bool` (deriving DecidableEq, Repr):
    a dynamic pinning obligation, its identity being its index in `S3.pins`.
  - Replace the field `S3.pin : Nat → Bool` by `pins : List PinOb`.
  - Define `S3.pin (s : S3) (l : Nat) : Bool := s.pins.any fun o => o.active && o.leaves.contains l`
    (a leaf is dynamically pinned while an active obligation covers it), so that existing uses
    `s.pin l = false` keep their meaning.

4	/-!
5	# Handle pool: a library instance of the access discipline (non-normative)
6	
7	**Non-normative.** This module formalizes the library contract "HandlePool v0.4 annex" (items
8	D.1–D.4), which `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` does not define (§75, Part XIV
9	preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
10	are not defined here"). The normative clauses that constrain it are
11	§36 (`MetaRight` is exercisable `Modify` on the administering value; `writeShared` alone is
12	insufficient), §37 and §89 (handles are data, not authorities), §38 and §46 (library state outside
13	`S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (the guard over all registries of live administrations)
14	and §58 (outcomes, statics before `fail`).
15	
16	The pool registry lives beside the kernel state (`PState`). Its operations are built on the
17	kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75): `newPool` registers only; `allocSlot` writes the handle into
18	its destination (O10); `resolve` derives a companion from `internal` over the whole storage, then
19	an entry authority from the companion (O1 twice); `resolveMany` does the same with `split` (O2) in
20	`Modify` and with one `Observe` derive per handle (O1) in `Observe`; `unresolve` releases (O3).
21	`freeSlot` applies the effect function of O12 (§69) to the slot content under preconditions that
22	exempt `internal` and its ancestors (`ContentEndPre`): it is not a kernel `endUse` step.
23	`contentEnd_preserves` proves that it preserves `KInv` (§57), and `contentEnd_preserves_kAux` that
24	it preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (not a clause of §57); `pstep_kernel` states what every pool step
25	is on the kernel side.
26	-/
27	
28	namespace Ern.Lib.HandlePool
29	
30	open Ern.MemoryModel
31	open Ern.MemoryModel.Access
32	
33	/-! ## Library state (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §38, §46) -/
34	
35	/-- Slot of a pool entry (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`;
36	non-normative library contract; §38, §46). -/
37	structure Slot where
38	  place : Nat
39	  gen : Nat
40	  live : Bool
41	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
42	
43	/-- Pool entry `{storage, internal, slots}` with its logical identity (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1;
44	non-normative library contract). The pool value is the place holding `internal` (§46 analogue). -/
45	structure Pool where
46	  id : Nat
47	  storage : Nat
48	  internal : Nat
49	  slots : List Slot
50	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
51	
52	/-- Handle `(poolId, slot, gen)`: data, not an authority (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §37, §89;
53	non-normative library contract). -/
54	structure Handle where
55	  id : Nat
56	  slot : Nat
57	  gen : Nat
58	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
59	
60	/-- Ghost record of a resolution (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; auxiliary information creating no
61	right, §38): pool identity and `internal`, the companion, the mode, and the entry authorities
62	tagged with their slot and resolved generation. Read only by `unresolve` and by the invariants. -/
63	structure Res where
64	  pool : Nat
65	  internal : Nat
66	  comp : Nat
67	  mode : Mode
68	  entries : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)
69	deriving DecidableEq, Repr
70	
71	/-- Library state (§38, §46; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative library contract): the
72	kernel state `S₃` and, separately, the pool registry, the next fresh pool identity and the ghost
73	resolutions. -/
74	structure PState where
75	  kern : S3
76	  pools : List Pool
77	  nId : Nat
78	  res : List Res
79	
80	/-- Initial library state (§47; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): the initial kernel state, an empty
81	registry. -/
82	def PState.init (statics : Statics) : PState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0, []⟩
83	
84	/-- The pool read as an arena entry with nothing available or issued, to reuse `MetaRight` of §36
85	(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library contract). -/
86	def Pool.entry (pl : Pool) : Arena.ArenaEntry := ⟨pl.storage, pl.internal, [], []⟩
87	
88	/-- Administrative right on the pool (§36; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, corrected by §36;
89	non-normative library contract): the pool is live (`internal` active) and `MetaRight` holds,
90	exercisable `Modify` over the pool value; no `writeShared` branch. -/
91	def AdminRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Prop := s.Active pl.internal ∧ Arena.MetaRight s pl.entry
92	
93	/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
94	instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Decidable (AdminRight s pl) := by
95	  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance
96	
97	/-- Place of slot `i`, `0` if absent (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative library
98	contract; §46). -/
99	def slotPlace (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Nat := ((pl.slots[i]?).map (·.place)).getD 0
100	
101	/-- The pool with slot `i` replaced (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library
102	contract; §46). -/
103	def setSlot (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : Pool := { pl with slots := pl.slots.set i sl }
104	
105	/-! ## `newPool` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §56) -/
106	
107	/-- The pool registry as a registry of live administrations (§56; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1;
108	non-normative library contract): the `internal` identities of its live pools. -/
109	def liveInternals (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) : List Nat :=
110	  (pools.filter fun pl => decide (s.Active pl.internal)).map (·.internal)
111	
112	/-- Preconditions of `newPool(storage, internal)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative
113	library contract; §56, §76). -/
114	structure NewPoolPre (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) (others : List (List Nat))
115	    (storage internal : Nat) : Prop where
116	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: "reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena`"
117	  (§76.1–§76.3, §76.5). -/
118	  base : Arena.NewArenaBase s storage internal
119	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: every leaf of the input storage is `Uninit`. -/
120	  uninit : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, s.I l = .uninit
121	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1, §56: `internal` is absent from the pool registry and from every
122	  other registry of live administrations `others`. -/
123	  guard : Arena.Guard56 (liveInternals s pools :: others) internal
124	
125	/-- Decidability of `NewPoolPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §56, §76). -/
126	instance (s : S3) (pools : List Pool) (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) :
127	    Decidable (NewPoolPre s pools others storage internal) :=
128	  decidable_of_iff (Arena.NewArenaBase s storage internal ∧
129	    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P storage, s.I l = .uninit) ∧
130	    Arena.Guard56 (liveInternals s pools :: others) internal)
131	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩⟩
132	
133	/-- Effect of `newPool` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative library contract): a pool with
134	the fresh identity `nId`, one free slot of generation zero per child of the storage, the kernel
135	state unchanged (§46, §76). -/
136	def newPoolEff (L : PState) (storage internal : Nat) : PState :=
137	  { L with
138	    pools := L.pools ++ [⟨L.nId, storage, internal,
139	      (kids L.kern.P storage).map fun q => ⟨q, 0, false⟩⟩]
140	    nId := L.nId + 1 }
141	
142	/-- `newPool` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §58; non-normative library contract):
143	`ok` or `reject`; `others` are the other registries of live administrations (§56). -/
144	def NewPoolStep (others : List (List Nat)) (storage internal : Nat) (L : PState) :
145	    Outcome3 PState → Prop :=
146	  Guarded (NewPoolPre L.kern L.pools others storage internal) (newPoolEff L storage internal)
147	
148	/-! ## `allocSlot` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3) -/
149	
150	/-- Static preconditions of `allocSlot(pool, dst)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, corrected by §36;
151	non-normative library contract). "Apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle" names no state
152	component and is not represented. -/
153	structure AllocSlotStatic (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (dst : Nat) : Prop where
154	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, §36: live pool and `MetaRight`. -/
155	  right : AdminRight s pl
156	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: `dst` is usable. -/
157	  dstUsable : s.Usable dst
158	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: `dst` is a leaf (the handle is written into "la seule feuille
159	  `dst`"). -/
160	  dstLeaf : isLeaf s.P dst
161	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3 with §67.1: the write of the handle needs exercisable `Modify`
162	  over `dst`. -/
163	  dstRight : HasRight s .modify dst
164	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: `dst` is not `Init`. -/
165	  dstNotInit : s.I dst ≠ .init
166	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: `dst` holds no active authority. -/
167	  dstFree : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
168	    OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True
169	
170	/-- Decidability of `AllocSlotStatic` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §36, §67). -/
171	instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (AllocSlotStatic s pl dst) :=
172	  decidable_of_iff (AdminRight s pl ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
173	    s.I dst ≠ .init ∧ ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
174	      OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True)
175	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩⟩
176	
177	/-- Effect of `allocSlot` on slot `i` of pool `j` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative
178	library contract): the slot becomes live with its generation kept; the handle is written into the
179	leaf `dst`, which alone becomes `Init` (§67 effect). -/
180	def allocSlotEff (L : PState) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) (dst : Nat) : PState :=
181	  { L with
182	    kern := write3Eff L.kern [dst]
183	    pools := L.pools.set j (setSlot pl i { sl with live := true }) }
184	
185	/-- The handle written by `allocSlot` for slot `i` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative
186	library contract; §37, §89). -/
187	def slotHandle (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Option Handle :=
188	  (pl.slots[i]?).map fun sl => ⟨pl.id, i, sl.gen⟩
189	
190	/-- `allocSlot(pool j, dst)` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §58; non-normative library
191	contract): `reject` without the pool or a static precondition; then `fail` when no slot is free;
192	`ok` on any free slot. -/
193	inductive AllocSlotStep (j dst : Nat) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
194	  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → AllocSlotStep j dst L .reject
195	  | static {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
196	      AllocSlotStep j dst L .reject
197	  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
198	      (∀ sl ∈ pl.slots, sl.live = true) → AllocSlotStep j dst L .fail
199	  | ok {pl : Pool} {i : Nat} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AllocSlotStatic L.kern pl dst →
200	      pl.slots[i]? = some sl → sl.live = false →
201	      AllocSlotStep j dst L (.ok (allocSlotEff L j pl i sl dst))
202	
203	/-! ## `resolve`, `resolveMany` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2) -/
204	
205	/-- The handle designates a live slot of the pool at its generation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2,
206	D.3; §89; non-normative library contract); a slot index outside the pool designates nothing. -/
207	def HandleOK (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Prop :=
208	  h.id = pl.id ∧ OptP (pl.slots[h.slot]?) (fun sl => sl.gen = h.gen ∧ sl.live = true) False
209	
210	/-- Decidability of `HandleOK` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §89). -/
211	instance (pl : Pool) (h : Handle) : Decidable (HandleOK pl h) := by
212	  unfold HandleOK; infer_instance
213	
214	/-- Legal exercise of `internal` at mode `m` for the companion (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2;
215	non-normative library contract): the preconditions of the `derive` of the companion from
216	`internal` over all leaves of the storage (§60). -/
217	def ResolveRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Prop :=
218	  DerivePre s pl.internal (footprint s.P pl.storage) m
219	
220	/-- Decidability of `ResolveRight` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60). -/
221	instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : Decidable (ResolveRight s pl m) := by
222	  unfold ResolveRight; infer_instance
223	
224	/-- State after the companion (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60 effect; non-normative library
225	contract): authority `|A|`, derived from `internal` at mode `m` over all leaves of the storage. -/
226	def compS (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (m : Mode) : S3 :=
227	  deriveEff s pl.internal (footprint s.P pl.storage) m
228	
229	/-- Observe derivations from `c`, one per region in order (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2:
230	`resolveMany` in `Observe`; §60; non-normative library contract): each accepted in the state left
231	by the previous ones. -/
232	def DerivesPre (s : S3) (c : Nat) : List (List Nat) → Prop
233	  | [] => True
234	  | r :: rs => DerivePre s c r .observe ∧ DerivesPre (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs
235	
236	/-- Decidability of `DerivesPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2, §60). -/
237	instance decDerivesPre (s : S3) (c : Nat) :
238	    (rs : List (List Nat)) → Decidable (DerivesPre s c rs)
239	  | [] => isTrue trivial
240	  | r :: rs =>
241	    have := decDerivesPre (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs
242	    inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))
243	
244	/-- Effect of the `Observe` derivations from `c`, in order (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60 effect).
245	-/
246	def derivesEff (s : S3) (c : Nat) : List (List Nat) → S3
247	  | [] => s
248	  | r :: rs => derivesEff (deriveEff s c r .observe) c rs
249	
250	/-- Entry authorities of a batch from the companion `c` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; non-normative
251	library contract): `split` (§61) in `Modify`, successive `Observe` derivations (§60) in
252	`Observe`. -/
253	def EntriesPre (k : K) : Mode → S3 → Nat → List (List Nat) → Prop
254	  | .modify, s, c, rs => SplitPre k s c rs
255	  | .observe, s, c, rs => DerivesPre s c rs
256	
257	/-- Decidability of `EntriesPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60, §61). -/
258	instance (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] (m : Mode) (s : S3) (c : Nat)
259	    (rs : List (List Nat)) : Decidable (EntriesPre k m s c rs) := by
260	  cases m <;> unfold EntriesPre <;> infer_instance
261	
262	/-- Effect of the entry authorities of a batch (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §60, §61 effects). -/
263	def entriesEff : Mode → S3 → Nat → List (List Nat) → S3
264	  | .modify, s, c, rs => splitEff s c rs
265	  | .observe, s, c, rs => derivesEff s c rs
266	
267	/-- Regions of the entries designated by a batch: the footprint of each slot
268	(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; non-normative library contract; §60). -/
269	def entryRegions (s : S3) (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) : List (List Nat) :=
270	  hs.map fun h => footprint s.P (slotPlace pl h.slot)
271	
272	/-- Ghost entries of a batch: the `n`-th entry authority is `c + 1 + n`, for slot and generation of
273	the `n`-th handle (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; auxiliary, §38). -/
274	def batchEntries (c : Nat) (hs : List Handle) : List (Nat × Nat × Nat) :=
275	  mapI (fun i h => (i, h.slot, h.gen)) (c + 1) hs
276	
277	/-- `resolve(h, m)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §58; non-normative
278	library contract): `reject` without the pool or the legal exercise of `internal`; then `fail` for
279	a handle of another pool, stale, absent or free; then the companion and the entry authority
280	derived from it, `reject` when the second derivation is not accepted. -/
281	inductive ResolveStep (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (m : Mode) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
282	  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → ResolveStep j h m L .reject
283	  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
284	      ResolveStep j h m L .reject
285	  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m → ¬ HandleOK pl h →
286	      ResolveStep j h m L .fail
287	  | noEntry {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
288	      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
289	      ¬ DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
290	      ResolveStep j h m L .reject
291	  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
292	      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
293	      DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
294	      ResolveStep j h m L (.ok { L with
295	        kern := deriveEff (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m
296	        res := L.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, L.kern.A.length, m,
297	          [(L.kern.A.length + 1, h.slot, h.gen)]⟩] })
298	
299	/-- Validity of a batch (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; non-normative library contract): every handle
300	designates a live slot at its generation; pairwise distinct slots in `Modify` only (§58, §89). -/
301	def BatchOK (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) : Prop :=
302	  (∀ h ∈ hs, HandleOK pl h) ∧ (m = .modify → (hs.map (·.slot)).Nodup)
303	
304	/-- Decidability of `BatchOK` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §58, §89). -/
305	instance (pl : Pool) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) : Decidable (BatchOK pl hs m) := by
306	  unfold BatchOK; infer_instance
307	
308	/-- `resolveMany(hs, m)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §58; non-normative
309	library contract): `reject` without the pool or the legal exercise of `internal`; then an atomic
310	`fail` for an invalid batch; then one companion and the entry authorities (`EntriesPre`), `reject`
311	when they are not accepted. -/
312	inductive ResolveManyStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (hs : List Handle) (m : Mode) (L : PState) :
313	    Outcome3 PState → Prop where
314	  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
315	  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
316	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
317	  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m → ¬ BatchOK pl hs m →
318	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .fail
319	  | noEntries {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m → BatchOK pl hs m →
320	      ¬ EntriesPre k m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs) →
321	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L .reject
322	  | ok {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m → BatchOK pl hs m →
323	      EntriesPre k m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs) →
324	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L (.ok { L with
325	        kern := entriesEff m (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (entryRegions L.kern pl hs)
326	        res := L.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, L.kern.A.length, m,
327	          batchEntries L.kern.A.length hs⟩] })

329	/-! ## `unresolve` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2) -/
330	
331	/-- Releases the authorities of a list in order (§62); `none` as soon as one release is not
332	accepted (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "Les règles de `release` … restent applicables"). -/
333	def releaseAll : S3 → List Nat → Option S3
334	  | s, [] => some s
335	  | s, a :: l => if ReleasePre s a then releaseAll (releaseEff s a) l else none
336	
337	/-- The resolution of companion `c` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; ghost lookup, §38). -/
338	def findRes (L : PState) (c : Nat) : Option Res := L.res.find? fun r => r.comp == c

340	/-- Authorities released by `unresolve` of `r` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; non-normative library
341	contract): the entry authorities still active, then the companion (§62). -/
342	def unresolveList (s : S3) (r : Res) : List Nat :=
343	  ((r.entries.map (·.1)).filter fun a => decide (s.Active a)) ++ [r.comp]
344	
345	/-- `unresolve(c)` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; §58; non-normative library
346	contract): the releases of `unresolveList`; `reject` when one is not accepted or `c` is no
347	companion. -/
348	inductive UnresolveStep (c : Nat) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
349	  | none : findRes L c = none → UnresolveStep c L .reject
350	  | reject {r : Res} : findRes L c = some r → releaseAll L.kern (unresolveList L.kern r) = none →
351	      UnresolveStep c L .reject
352	  | ok {r : Res} {s' : S3} : findRes L c = some r →
353	      releaseAll L.kern (unresolveList L.kern r) = some s' →
354	      UnresolveStep c L (.ok { L with kern := s' })

356	/-! ## `freeSlot` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3) -/
357	
358	/-- `x` is exempt from the end-of-use checks of a slot of the pool of `internal` `i`: `internal` or
359	one of its ancestors (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "hors `internal` et ses ancêtres"; non-normative
360	library contract; §69). -/
361	def Exempt (s : S3) (i x : Nat) : Prop := x = i ∨ x ∈ s.ancs i
362	
363	/-- Decidability of `Exempt` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69). -/
364	instance (s : S3) (i x : Nat) : Decidable (Exempt s i x) := by unfold Exempt; infer_instance
365	
366	/-- §69.2 for storage that dies with the content (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: the end-of-use
367	effects of O12; non-normative library contract): an active derived authority over a leaf of a place
368	that stops being usable is held within the slot `q` or by a dying holder. -/
369	def DyingAccessOK (s : S3) (q j : Nat) : Prop :=
370	  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.origin ≠ none →
371	    (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, isLeaf s.P l ∧ s.Usable l ∧ ¬ (endUseS s q).Usable l) →
372	      heldIn s.P q y.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (endUseS s q) y.holder) True
373	
374	/-- Decidability of `DyingAccessOK` (§69.2; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
375	instance (s : S3) (q j : Nat) : Decidable (DyingAccessOK s q j) := by
376	  unfold DyingAccessOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance
377	
378	/-- §69.3 with the exemption of D.3 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library contract):
379	anchor `x` of a place remaining usable is not held within the slot `q` and keeps a live holder;
380	unless exempt, it is not a root of `q`. -/
381	def ContentAnchorOK (s : S3) (q i x : Nat) : Prop :=
382	  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ heldIn s.P q y.holder ∧ (¬ Exempt s i x → ¬ IsRootOf s q y) ∧
383	    HolderLive (endUseS s q) y.holder) True
384	
385	/-- Decidability of `ContentAnchorOK` (§69.3; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
386	instance (s : S3) (q i x : Nat) : Decidable (ContentAnchorOK s q i x) := by
387	  unfold ContentAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance
388	
389	/-- Preconditions of the end of the content of slot place `q` of the pool of `internal` `i`
390	(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible"; the preconditions
391	of O12, §69, excluding `internal` and its ancestors; non-normative library contract). §69.1 is not
392	a precondition: `freeSlot_modify_right` derives it from `AdminRight`. -/
393	structure ContentEndPre (k : K) (s : S3) (q i : Nat) : Prop where
394	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: no active authority covers the entry except `internal` and its
395	  ancestors (§69.2 on the leaves of the entry, with the exemption). -/
396	  entry : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active j → (∃ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∈ footprint s.P q) →
397	    Exempt s i j
398	  /-- §69.2 on the storage that dies with the content (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
399	  dying : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, DyingAccessOK s q j
400	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, §69.3: no usable dependency is invalidated. -/

400	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, §69.3: no usable dependency is invalidated. -/
401	  anchors : ∀ q' ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s q).Usable q' →
402	    ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s q).D q', ContentAnchorOK s q i x
403	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, §69.4: no ending leaf is pinned, statically or dynamically. -/
404	  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s q l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l
405	
406	/-- Decidability of `ContentEndPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69). -/
407	instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (q i : Nat) :
408	    Decidable (ContentEndPre k s q i) :=
409	  decidable_of_iff ((∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active j →
410	      (∃ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∈ footprint s.P q) → Exempt s i j) ∧
411	    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, DyingAccessOK s q j) ∧
412	    (∀ q' ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s q).Usable q' →
413	      ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s q).D q', ContentAnchorOK s q i x) ∧
414	    (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s q l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l))
415	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩⟩
416	
417	/-- Effect of `freeSlot` on slot `i` of pool `j` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library
418	contract): the effects of O12 on the slot content (`endUseEff`, §69), no deallocation; the slot
419	becomes free and its generation is incremented. -/
420	def freeSlotEff (L : PState) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : PState :=
421	  { L with
422	    kern := endUseEff L.kern sl.place
423	    pools := L.pools.set j (setSlot pl i ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) }
424	
425	/-- `freeSlot(h)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, corrected by §36; §58;
426	non-normative library contract): `reject` without the pool, without a live pool or `MetaRight`;
427	then `fail` for a handle of another pool, stale, absent or free; then `reject` unless the end of
428	the content is admissible (`ContentEndPre`). -/
429	inductive FreeSlotStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
430	  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
431	  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AdminRight L.kern pl →
432	      FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
433	  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl → ¬ HandleOK pl h →
434	      FreeSlotStep k j h L .fail
435	  | noEnd {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
436	      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ¬ ContentEndPre k L.kern sl.place pl.internal →
437	      FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
438	  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
439	      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ContentEndPre k L.kern sl.place pl.internal →
440	      FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok (freeSlotEff L j pl h.slot sl))

442	/-! ## Library runs (HandlePool v0.4 annex; §38, §46, §57) -/
443	
444	/-- One `ok` step of a library run (HandlePool v0.4 annex; non-normative library contract): a
445	kernel step O1–O16 of non-administrative code, the registry unchanged, or an accepted pool
446	operation (§57, §58). -/
447	inductive PStep (k : K) : PState → PState → Prop where
448	  | kernel {L : PState} {s' : S3} : KStep k L.kern s' → PStep k L { L with kern := s' }
449	  | newPool {L L' : PState} {others : List (List Nat)} {st i : Nat} :
450	      NewPoolStep others st i L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
451	  | allocSlot {L L' : PState} {j dst : Nat} : AllocSlotStep j dst L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
452	  | resolve {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} {m : Mode} :
453	      ResolveStep j h m L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
454	  | resolveMany {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {hs : List Handle} {m : Mode} :
455	      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
456	  | unresolve {L L' : PState} {c : Nat} : UnresolveStep c L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
457	  | freeSlot {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
458	      PStep k L L'
459	
460	/-- Library states reachable from the initial library state (§47) by library steps
461	(HandlePool v0.4 annex; non-normative library contract). -/
462	inductive PReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : PState → Prop where
463	  | init : PReach k statics (PState.init statics)
464	  | step {L L' : PState} : PReach k statics L → PStep k L L' → PReach k statics L'
465	
466	/-- Library runs in which every step starts from a kernel state satisfying `KInv`
467	(§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex). Under the guarantee of §57 every library-reachable state is such a
468	state (`PReach.toI`); the pool theorems are stated on these runs, so that they do not depend on
469	that guarantee. -/
470	inductive PReachI (k : K) (statics : Statics) : PState → Prop where
471	  | init : PReachI k statics (PState.init statics)
472	  | step {L L' : PState} : PReachI k statics L → KInv L.kern → PStep k L L' →
473	      PReachI k statics L'
474	
475	/-- Kernel side of library runs (§57, §69 effect; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): a kernel step
476	O1–O16, or the end of the content of a slot place `q` under `ContentEndPre` for some `internal`
477	`i`. -/
478	inductive XStep (k : K) : S3 → S3 → Prop where
479	  | kernel {s s' : S3} : KStep k s s' → XStep k s s'
480	  | contentEnd {s : S3} {q i : Nat} : ContentEndPre k s q i → XStep k s (endUseEff s q)
481	
482	/-- States reachable from `S3.init statics` by `XStep` (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
483	inductive XReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : S3 → Prop where
484	  | init : XReach k statics (S3.init statics)
485	  | step {s s' : S3} : XReach k statics s → XStep k s s' → XReach k statics s'
486	
487	/-- Finite sequences of kernel steps O1–O16 (§57, §58; HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
488	inductive KSeq (k : K) : S3 → S3 → Prop where
489	  | refl (s : S3) : KSeq k s s
490	  | tail {s s₁ s₂ : S3} : KSeq k s s₁ → KStep k s₁ s₂ → KSeq k s s₂

492	/-! ## The end of a slot content preserves the kernel invariant (§57, §69; D.3) -/
493	
494	/-- Under `ContentEndPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, §69.3 with the exemption) and `I3` (§52),
495	every anchor of a place usable after `endUseS` stays active after the end of the content. -/
496	theorem contentEnd_anchors {k : K} {s : S3} {q i : Nat} (h3 : I3 s)
497	    (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) :
498	    ∀ q', (endUseS s q).Usable q' → ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s q).D q', (endUseEff s q).Active x := by
499	  intro q' hq x hx
500	  have hq₀ := EndFree.endUseS_usable hq
501	  have hx₀ : x ∈ s.D q' := by
502	    simp only [endUseS] at hx; split at hx
503	    · simp at hx
504	    · exact hx
505	  obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := h3 q' hq₀ x hx₀
506	  have hc := hpre.anchors q' (List.mem_range.2 hq₀.lt) hq x hx
507	  unfold ContentAnchorOK OptP at hc; rw [hy] at hc
508	  obtain ⟨hnh, -, hl⟩ := hc
509	  exact ⟨y, by rw [endUseEff, EndFree.cleanup_get, EndFree.endUseS_get, hy]; simp [hnh, hl], ya⟩
510	
511	/-- The end of the content preserves `NoDangling` (§54, §69; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3), under
512	`WF3` (§49) and `I1` (§50): an active authority on a leaf of a place that stops being usable is
513	derived, and blocked by §69.2 on dying storage, or a root, held by the owner of the root place of
514	the leaf (`rootHeldConv_active`), which stays usable. -/
515	theorem contentEnd_noDangling {k : K} {s : S3} {q i : Nat} (hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s)
516	    (h1 : I1 s) (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) (hw' : WF3 (endUseEff s q)) :
517	    NoDangling (endUseEff s q) := by
518	  have hU := EndFree.cleanup_usable (endUseS s q)
519	  intro j z hz za q' hq l hl hlz
520	  obtain ⟨hz₀, hnh, hlive⟩ := EndFree.endUse_active hz za
521	  by_cases hq₀ : ¬ s.Usable q'
522	  · exact hnd j z hz₀ za q' hq₀ l hl hlz
523	  replace hq₀ := Decidable.of_not_not hq₀
524	  obtain ⟨-, hleaf, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
525	  have hl₀ : s.Usable l := usable_of_partOf hw (l + 1) l q' (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlq hq₀
526	  have hl₁ : ¬ (endUseS s q).Usable l := fun hu => hq (usable_of_part hw' hlq ((hU l).2 hu))
527	  cases hzo : z.origin with
528	  | some o =>
529	    have hacc := hpre.dying j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz₀))
530	    unfold DyingAccessOK OptP at hacc; rw [hz₀] at hacc
531	    rcases hacc za (by rw [hzo]; simp) ⟨l, hlz, hleaf, hl₀, hl₁⟩ with e | e
532	    · exact hnh e
533	    · exact e hlive
534	  | none =>
535	    obtain ⟨-, -, r, -, -, -, hr, hlr, -⟩ := hw.rootChain j z l hz₀ hlz hleaf
536	    obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hh⟩ := rootHeldConv_active hw h1 hnd j z l r hz₀ za hzo hlz hr hlr
537	    have hnown : ¬ OwnedIn s.P q r := fun hown => by
538	      cases hown with
539	      | @direct _ o _ hpl ho hpart =>
540	        have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
541	        rw [hh, e] at hnh; exact hnh hpart
542	      | @step _ o _ hpl ho hown' =>
543	        have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
544	        rw [hh, e] at hlive
545	        have := EndFree.dead_false hlive
546	        simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at this
547	        exact this.2 hown'
548	    have hd : (endUseS s q).dead r = false := by
549	      simp only [endUseS, ← hw.deadOf hlr, EndFree.dead_false hl₀, Bool.false_or,
550	        decide_eq_false_iff_not]
551	      exact hnown
552	    have hr₁ : (endUseS s q).Usable r := EndFree.usable_of_owner hpr hd (hh ▸ hlive)
553	    exact hl₁ ((hU l).1 (usable_of_partOf hw' (l + 1) l r (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlr ((hU r).2 hr₁)))
554	
555	/-- The end of the content of a slot place `q` under `ContentEndPre` preserves the kernel invariant
556	`KInv` (§57) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "la correspondance des effets et la préservation des
557	invariants sous ce droit constituent une obligation explicite de reconstruction"; §69 effect); the auxiliary `KAux` is preserved by
558	`contentEnd_preserves_kAux`. -/
559	theorem contentEnd_preserves {k : K} {s : S3} {q i : Nat} (hk : KInv s)
560	    (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) : KInv (endUseEff s q) := by
561	  have hw := hk.1
562	  refine EndFree.releases_preserve hk (EndFree.endUseS_releases s q) rfl rfl rfl
563	    (fun q h => by simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff] at h; exact h.1)
564	    (fun q' pl r hq hp => ?_) (fun q' _ x hx => ?_) (contentEnd_anchors hk.2.1.1.2.2.1 hpre)
565	    (fun r n z pr _ hur hz _ _ hpr hzh _ => ?_)
566	    (contentEnd_noDangling hw hk.2.1.2.2 hk.2.1.1.1 hpre)
567	  · obtain ⟨-, -, -, -, hd⟩ := hw.places q' pl r hq hp
568	    simp only [endUseS, hd, decide_eq_decide.2 (EndFree.ownedIn_parent hw hq hp)]
569	  · simp only [endUseS] at hx; split at hx
570	    · simp at hx
571	    · exact hx
572	  · have hnh : ¬ heldIn s.P q z.holder := fun hh => by
573	      have hd := EndFree.dead_false hur
574	      simp only [endUseS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at hd
575	      rw [hzh] at hh
576	      cases ho : pr.owner with
577	      | frame f => rw [ho] at hh; exact hh
578	      | place o => rw [ho] at hh; exact hd.2 (.direct hpr ho hh)
579	    rw [EndFree.endUseS_get, hz]; simp [hnh]
580	
581	/-- The end of the content of a slot place `q` preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (`RootHeldConv`, §40,
582	§49.7; not a clause of §57) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69 effect: places are unchanged and
583	authorities are only released). -/
584	theorem contentEnd_preserves_kAux {s : S3} {q : Nat} (ha : KAux s) : KAux (endUseEff s q) :=
585	  EndFree.releases_preserve_kAux ha (EndFree.endUseS_releases s q) rfl

587	/-! ## Kernel side of the pool operations (§57, §58; HandlePool v0.4 annex) -/

589	/-- Sequences of kernel steps compose (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
590	theorem KSeq.trans {k : K} {s₁ s₂ s₃ : S3} (h₁ : KSeq k s₁ s₂) (h₂ : KSeq k s₂ s₃) :
591	    KSeq k s₁ s₃ := by
592	  induction h₂ with
593	  | refl => exact h₁
594	  | tail _ hs ih => exact .tail ih hs

596	/-- One kernel step is a sequence (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
597	theorem KSeq.single {k : K} {s s' : S3} (h : KStep k s s') : KSeq k s s' := .tail (.refl s) h
598	
599	/-- `releaseAll` is a sequence of `release` steps (§62; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2). -/
600	theorem releaseAll_kseq {k : K} : ∀ {s s' : S3} {l : List Nat}, releaseAll s l = some s' →
601	    KSeq k s s'
602	  | s, s', [], h => by simp only [releaseAll, Option.some.injEq] at h; subst h; exact .refl s
603	  | s, s', a :: l, h => by
604	    simp only [releaseAll] at h
605	    split at h
606	    · rename_i hpre
607	      exact (KSeq.single (.release (Guarded.ok hpre))).trans (releaseAll_kseq h)
608	    · cases h

610	/-- The `Observe` derivations of `resolveMany` are a sequence of `derive` steps
611	(§60; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2). -/
612	theorem derives_kseq {k : K} {c : Nat} : ∀ {s : S3} {rs : List (List Nat)}, DerivesPre s c rs →
613	    KSeq k s (derivesEff s c rs)
614	  | s, [], _ => .refl s
615	  | _, _ :: _, ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ => (KSeq.single (.derive (Guarded.ok h₁))).trans (derives_kseq h₂)
616	
617	/-- The entry authorities of `resolveMany` are a `split` (§61) or a sequence of `derive` steps
618	(§60) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2). -/
619	theorem entries_kseq {k : K} {m : Mode} {s : S3} {c : Nat} {rs : List (List Nat)}
620	    (h : EntriesPre k m s c rs) : KSeq k s (entriesEff m s c rs) := by
621	  cases m with
622	  | modify => exact KSeq.single (.split (Guarded.ok h))
623	  | observe => exact derives_kseq h

625	/-- Under `KInv` (§57), exercisable `Modify` over a usable leaf gives the preconditions of an
626	ordinary write of that leaf (§67; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: the write of the handle). -/
627	theorem write_of_right {s : S3} (hk : KInv s) {dst : Nat} (hu : s.Usable dst)
628	    (hl : isLeaf s.P dst) (hr : HasRight s .modify dst) : ∃ a, Write3Pre s a [dst] := by
629	  obtain ⟨a, -, hex, hall⟩ := hr

653	      obtain ⟨a, hw⟩ := write_of_right hk hst.dstUsable hst.dstLeaf hst.dstRight
654	      exact .inl (KSeq.single (.write (a := a) (Guarded.ok hw)))

659	  | resolveMany hs =>

912	(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1, D.3; auxiliary information, §38). -/

915	  storage : Nat
916	  internal : Nat

929	the footprint of the storage (§76.2, §76.3); the storage and every slot have a leaf; slots lie in
930	the storage and are pairwise disjoint (D.1). -/
931	structure PoolOK (s : S3) (sh : PoolShape) : Prop where
932	  /-- §76.2: `internal` exists, with own mode `Modify` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
933	  internalMode : OptP (s.A[sh.internal]?) (fun y => y.mode = .modify) False
934	  /-- §76.3: `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
935	  fpEq : ∀ l, l ∈ s.afp sh.internal ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P sh.storage
936	  /-- §40, §49.2: the storage has a leaf (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
937	  storageLeaf : ∃ l, l ∈ footprint s.P sh.storage
938	  /-- §40, §49.2: every slot has a leaf (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
939	  slotLeaf : ∀ q ∈ sh.places, ∃ l, l ∈ footprint s.P q
940	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: slots lie in the storage. -/

948	resolution, over the footprint of the storage; each entry authority is younger than the companion,
949	over the footprint of its slot (§38, §60). -/
950	def ResOK (s : S3) (shs : List PoolShape) (r : Res) : Prop :=
951	  ∃ sh ∈ shs, sh.id = r.pool ∧ sh.internal = r.internal ∧ r.internal < r.comp ∧
952	    OptP (s.A[r.comp]?) (fun y => y.mode = r.mode ∧
953	      ∀ l, l ∈ y.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P sh.storage) False ∧
954	    ∀ e ∈ r.entries, r.comp < e.1 ∧ ∃ q, sh.places[e.2.1]? = some q ∧

957	/-- Ghost well-formedness of the pool layer (auxiliary, not a clause of the contract;
958	HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1, D.2): fresh distinct identities, well-formed pools and resolutions
959	(§38). -/
960	structure PoolWF (L : PState) : Prop where

963	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: identities are distinct. -/

965	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: every pool is well formed. -/

967	  /-- HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: every ghost resolution is well formed. -/
968	  res : ∀ r ∈ L.res, ResOK L.kern (L.pools.map Pool.shape) r

971	library contract): no active entry authority designates a free slot or a former generation (§89). -/
972	def NoStale (L : PState) : Prop :=

974	    ∃ sl, pl.slots[e.2.1]? = some sl ∧ sl.gen = e.2.2 ∧ sl.live = true

978	contract's sentence also covers the companions of other pools (`ModifyExclusive`). -/

980	  ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → r₁.comp ≠ r₂.comp →
981	    L.kern.Active r₁.comp → L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .observe ∧ r₂.mode = .observe

984	def FpKeep (s s' : S3) : Prop :=
985	  ∀ q l₀, l₀ ∈ footprint s.P q → ∀ l, l ∈ footprint s'.P q ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P q

988	theorem fpKeep_of_P {s s' : S3} (h : s'.P = s.P) : FpKeep s s' := fun _ _ _ _ => by rw [h]

1020	    this p hp (.inl rfl)
1021	  intro q hq

1024	    intro hc

1046	  refine ⟨optP_false_iff.2 ⟨y', hy', m'.trans hym⟩, fun l => ?_, ⟨l₀, (hst l₀).2 hl₀⟩,

1102	  obtain ⟨y, hy, -⟩ := optP_false_iff.1 hc

1114	    (hA : Arena.AKeep L.kern s') : CompExcl { L with kern := s' } :=

1119	(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §46). -/

1122	  | [], _, _, _, ha, _, _ => by simp at ha
1123	  | c :: l, a, b, hn, ha, hb, he => by
1124	    rw [List.map_cons, List.nodup_cons] at hn
1125	    rcases List.mem_cons.1 ha with ha' | ha' <;> rcases List.mem_cons.1 hb with hb' | hb'
1126	    · rw [ha', hb']

1128	    · subst hb'; exact absurd (he.symm ▸ List.mem_map_of_mem (f := (·.id)) ha') hn.1

# Annexe D — Instance `HandlePool` (non normative, contrat de bibliothèque)

Cette annexe décrit une **instance de bibliothèque** de la discipline MM-03, et non une nouvelle opération primitive du langage. Les noms sont sémantiques. Le contrat doit être reconstruit et vérifié ; les résultats du jalon 3 concernent le modèle exploratoire et ses conditions, **pas** automatiquement les règles corrigées ci-dessous.

## D.1 — Identité, état et stockage

Un handle est une donnée `(poolId, slot, gen)` **sans autorité d'accès intrinsèque**. L'identité logique `poolId` est fraîche et n'est pas réutilisée pendant l'exécution pertinente : détruire puis recréer un pool à la même adresse ne réactive pas un ancien handle. Chaque pool vivant conserve une entrée abstraite `{storage, internal, slots}`, où chaque slot possède `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`. Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage` ; leur métadonnée abstraite est représentée en octets par l'implémentation de bibliothèque.

`storage` peut être local, statique, alloué ou être un bloc issu d'une arène. **`newPool(storage, internal)` exige que toutes les feuilles du stockage d'entrée soient `Uninit`** et doit vérifier la garde unifiée de MM-03.3 §2.7 bis sur les deux registres des abstractions vivantes. Il reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena` sans fabriquer ni droits ni initialisation des valeurs de slots. Les entrées libres sont `Uninit` ; leur génération initiale est zéro. Une autorité ne peut être `internal` de deux abstractions vivantes, et une arène ne peut réutiliser l'`internal` d'un pool vivant.

## D.2 — Emprunt composé et résolution

Une résolution réussie dérive **de `internal` une autorité compagne** couvrant toutes les feuilles du stockage du pool, de mode `Observe` ou `Modify`, puis dérive **de cette compagne** une autorité de même mode par entrée résolue. L'autorité d'entrée est une descendante de la compagne, et non une autre dérivation indépendante de `internal`. Les deux sont soumises aux règles ordinaires de modes effectifs, d'exercice, de détention, d'ancrage et de transfert ; aucune permission nouvelle n'est créée.

`resolve(h, Observe | Modify)` vérifie l'identité de pool, la génération et la vivacité du slot **avant toute création d'autorité** : handle d'un autre pool, périmé, slot absent ou libre ⇒ `fail`, sans changement d'état. Une résolution valide exige l'exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis. Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool ; des compagnes `Observe` peuvent coexister. Il est impossible de libérer une compagne tant que ses descendantes d'entrée sont actives (O3.2). La propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau, pas seulement deux appels successifs de `resolve`.

`resolveMany(handles, Modify)` crée **une** compagne `Modify` et une autorité `Modify` par entrée. La distinction des slots est vérifiée dynamiquement pour ce lot ; toute identité invalide, génération périmée, entrée libre ou répétition de slot donne `fail` **atomique**, sans création partielle de droits. `resolveMany(handles, Observe)` utilise des dérivations `Observe` de la compagne `Observe`, **sans `split` ni contrôle de distinction** : la répétition du même handle valide est permise. Les `reject` de discipline d'accès restent distincts des `fail` de validation des handles.

`unresolve` libère d'abord toutes les dérivées d'entrée encore actives, puis la compagne. Les règles de `release`, y compris celles qui empêchent la libération en présence de descendants ou d'ancres valides, restent applicables ; le contrat ne supprime pas silencieusement des autorités transférées.

## D.3 — Allocation et fin d'usage de slot

`allocSlot(pool, dst)` exige un pool vivant, l'autorisation d'administration de ses métadonnées, une destination utilisable et libre d'autorité active, non `Init`, apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle. `fail` si aucun slot libre ; `ok` choisit un slot libre, le rend vivant, conserve sa génération et écrit son handle dans la seule feuille `dst`, selon les obligations de représentation (Spec 4) et d'ABI (Spec 11). **Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit`** jusqu'à son écriture ; l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot.

`freeSlot(h)` exige un pool **vivant** et `MetaRight`, c'est-à-dire le droit légal d'administration de la valeur pool par `Modify` exerçable ou par mutation `writeShared` admissible de ses métadonnées `SharedMutable`. `fail` si l'identité ou la génération ne correspond pas ; un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité. Pour réussir, la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible : **aucune dépendance utilisable** ne serait invalidée, **aucune feuille n'est épinglée**, et **aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres**. En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée. Le contrôle n'interprète pas `internal` comme un emprunt externe empêchant systématiquement le nettoyage de ses propres slots.

L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`, remet les feuilles de l'entrée à `Uninit`, marque l'entrée libre et incrémente sa génération ; **il ne désalloue pas implicitement l'allocation MM-02 du stockage**. Il ne s'agit pas de supposer une invocation de O12 autorisée par simple `MetaRight` : la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une **obligation explicite de reconstruction**, notamment dans les cas `writeShared`.

## D.4 — Invariant corrigé et limites

`PoolInv` exige : (1) les entrées sont deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; (2) aucune autorité d'entrée active ne désigne un slot libre ou une ancienne génération (`pool_no_stale_access`) ; (3) **garantie de transition** : `freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné. La dernière clause concerne le succès des transitions, non une interdiction globale de toutes les dérivations du noyau sur des slots libres. Les dérivations ordinaires issues d'une autorité d'entrée restent permises par le noyau.

Les générations sont des entiers naturels dans le modèle abstrait. Leur débordement ou leur recyclage dans une représentation finie doivent être empêchés par l'implémentation (par exemple retrait définitif d'un slot) ; l'ABI est spécifiée en Spec 11. L'encapsulation qui empêche un client d'accéder directement à une compagne administrative appartient à la Spec 9. Les handles persistants peuvent représenter des liens cycliques ; les résolutions qui en découlent restent temporaires et soumises à MM-03.

**Statut des preuves :** le jalon 3 rapporte `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, `pool_no_stale_access`, `pool_resolveMany_atomic`, `pool_resolveMany_distinct`, `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` et `pool_entries_disjoint` sur son brouillon, sous les hypothèses détaillées dans `J3_v0.1.md`. Il rapporte également un contre-exemple à l'ancienne formulation de `pool_inv_preserved`. **Il ne constitue pas encore la preuve** de la nouvelle règle `freeSlot` sous `MetaRight` ni de la totalité du contrat corrigé : ces obligations sont consignées en annexe F.

# Annexe E — Registre inter-spécifications (non normatif pour la Spec 1)

| Destination | Obligations ouvertes ou précisées |
|---|---|
| **Spec 2 — Concurrence** | Partie concurrente de `stat` ; `writeShared` et synchronisation ; transférabilité, partageabilité, suspension concurrente ; cas H39, H41. |
| **Spec 3 — Contrôle de flux et appels** | Protection forte de paramètres (`Reach`, `lineage`, `derivedIn`, G1', A3 strict) ; ré-emprunt d'un paramètre `Modify` par un paramètre dérivé `Observe` (H01, admis dans le noyau séquentiel, sans promettre la protection forte) ; **passage par valeur (`sink`) vers l'appelé** : prévoir la primitive MM-03 correspondante, transfert d'un emplacement de l'appelant vers un local de l'appelé au moment de l'entrée, sans affaiblir arbitrairement O4 ; retour et `defer` (H16, H27b, H38, H40, H42). |
| **Spec 4 — Types** | Validité de représentation (`dec`), `SameSizeAlong`, information de forme pour des régions non contiguës, feuille de destination d'une référence typée, correspondance `kind` et type ; **mémoire rendue par une abstraction de réutilisation (bloc d'arène réémis, entrée de pool) exposée comme typée non initialisée jusqu'à écriture explicite**, sans réinterprétation implicite d'anciens octets. La décision ne change pas rétroactivement les effets d'initialisation de `reset` sur l'état abstrait MM-03. |
| **Spec 9 — Encapsulation** | Empêcher l'usage extérieur des autorités internes/compagnes administratives des bibliothèques sûres. |
